## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/progress ``` **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — transitive registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | progress | `@components/cadence/progress/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/progress.json) | [Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) [Source files: progress](https://cadence.dev/r/progress.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once: ```tsx import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider"; export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return {children}; } ``` Copy all nine target files, keeping `progress/index.tsx` beside the shared `lib/` directory, the relative imports intact and the sources' `"use client"` directives. Progress imports `NativeControlDiv` from `control-animation.tsx`, which also reaches `native-div.tsx` and `press-button.tsx`. Copy the complete provider, motion and utilities payloads, even without a provider wrapper. The provider files and `motion` package remain required imports. Complete the base theme setup linked above and ensure Tailwind scans the copied files. Progress needs no additional item-specific CSS, icon package or external asset. Its full-width indicator uses `scaleX` for determinate updates through `data.transition`; reduced and none jump to the new fraction. A null value uses the theme's opacity-only `animate-pulse` in full and reduced, and `animate-none` in none. Continuous loops follow the theme animation token, not the provider speed. Standalone bars follow the system motion preference; an optional `CadenceProvider` controls a subtree, and nested full still respects system reduced motion. Usage, the top specimen, Labelled, Indeterminate, Complete, Custom range, Composed track and Explicit motion scopes use only Progress and its included helpers. Caller-owned progress also needs [Button](/components/button): ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button ``` For manual installation, follow Button's Manual tab and add `button/index.tsx`. Its shared files and Base UI package are already included above; its additional npm dependency is: ```package-manager npm install class-variance-authority ``` No example needs another package or external asset. The site's preview shell is not consumer setup. In Next.js App Router, Usage, Labelled, Indeterminate, Complete, Composed track and the top specimen can be composed in synchronous Server Components with the shown serializable props. Custom range needs a caller client module for its function-valued `getAriaValueText`. Caller-owned progress and Explicit motion scopes need one for `useState` and slider change handlers; the former also handles a button click. Synchronous `useId` alone does not require a client boundary. Caller refs, event handlers, function-valued `render`, `className(state)`, `style(state)` or `ProgressValue` children also need a caller client boundary. Preserve the installed sources' client directives. Supply a finite numeric `value` within a finite `min`/`max` range with `max > min`, or explicitly pass `null` for indeterminate work. The default range is zero to 100; there is no `defaultValue` or automatic progress source. The fill fraction is `(value - min) / (max - min)`, clamped to zero through one. At the maximum, Base UI exposes the complete state. `ProgressValue` displays the normalized percentage by default, so three of five displays 60%; `format` and `locale` configure number formatting. `getAriaValueText(formatted, raw)` customizes the accessible value text without changing the fill or visible value. For null, Base UI omits `aria-valuenow` and the default visible value is empty; provide meaningful loading text separately. `Progress` appends its own track and indicator after its children. Put `ProgressLabel` and `ProgressValue` inside the root. Adding a `ProgressTrack` with `ProgressIndicator` creates an additional track sharing the same fraction, as Composed track shows; it does not replace the default. Keep the indicator's full width and transform ownership when styling it. A custom indicator `render` replaces the animation adapter, so the caller must preserve its motion contract. The root owns `role="progressbar"` and its range/value ARIA attributes, not the track. Give it an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, or let the nested `ProgressLabel` register its association after hydration. Use an explicit root name when it must already be associated in server/no-JS markup. `ProgressValue` is visible text with `aria-hidden`; the root supplies the accessible value. The default bar has no tab stop, keyboard value editing, hidden form input or submission value. Native props, refs and Base UI `render` belong to their respective parts; retain the supplied props and ref when replacing an element. Put cancellation or retry in separate controls. The caller owns the real work, progress reports, range policy, loading/error text, completion announcement, cancellation, retries and persistence. A value of 100 in the default range only renders completion; it does not finish or validate an upload, submit a form or announce a live status by itself. ## Usage ```tsx import { Progress } from "@/components/cadence/progress"; export function Upload() { return ; } ``` `value` is required and may be `null` for indeterminate work. `Progress` renders its own track and indicator; `ProgressLabel` and `ProgressValue` go inside it as children. ## Labelled, with the number ProgressLabel supplies the accessible name and ProgressValue formats the same value as a percentage. The label and number remain readable above the default track. This loop remains under reduced motion, stops under none and follows the theme animation token rather than the provider speed. ```tsx import { Progress, ProgressLabel } from "@/components/cadence/progress"; export function IndeterminateProgress() { return ( Preparing preview ); } ``` ## Complete A fixed completed task shows 100% and a separate status message. The caller supplies the completion announcement; a filled progressbar alone is not a live notification. ```tsx import { Progress, ProgressLabel, ProgressValue } from "@/components/cadence/progress"; export function CompleteProgress() { return (
Upload complete

All files uploaded.

); } ``` ## Custom range Three completed steps in a five-step range render a 60% fill. The caller provides a more specific accessible value text without changing the numeric fraction. ```tsx "use client"; import { Progress, ProgressValue } from "@/components/cadence/progress"; export function CustomProgressRange() { return ( "Step 3 of 5"} className="max-w-sm" > ); } ``` ## Composed track A custom track is added alongside the default track, matching the root composition. Both indicators read the same fraction. This example compares a six-pixel custom track with the default eight-pixel track; it does not replace the default. ```tsx import { Progress, ProgressIndicator, ProgressTrack } from "@/components/cadence/progress"; export function ComposedProgress() { return ( ); } ``` ## Caller-owned progress The slider represents external upload reports; Complete upload supplies a final value. The caller owns updates and completion text. No timer invents progress, and none of these updates changes another example. ```tsx "use client"; import { useId, useState } from "react"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { Progress, ProgressLabel, ProgressValue } from "@/components/cadence/progress"; export function CallerProgress() { const id = useId(); const [value, setValue] = useState(62); return (

{value === 100 ? "Upload complete" : `Uploaded ${value}%`}

); } ``` ## Explicit motion scopes The first indeterminate indicator is fixed to none from its first DOM appearance, with no opacity loop. The second bar explicitly requests full within that outer none scope; its external slider changes only that value, and system reduced motion still wins. Ordinary bars inherit the header. ```tsx "use client"; import { useId, useState } from "react"; import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider"; import { Progress } from "@/components/cadence/progress"; export function StaticProgress() { const id = useId(); const [value, setValue] = useState(20); return (
); } ``` ## When to use - Work with a measurable end: an upload, an import, a multi-step build. - Work long enough that the user would otherwise wonder whether anything is happening, and short enough that they will watch the bar. - A determinate value next to other numbers, where the bar is a second reading of the same fact. ## When not to use - Work of unknown duration. Pass `value={null}` for an indeterminate bar, or use `spinner` when there is no bar to fill. - A page that is simply loading its own content; use `skeleton`. - A value that is not progressing toward an end, like a score. Render the number. ## API ### `Progress` | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- | | `value` | `number \| null` | – | Required. `null` means indeterminate. | | `min`, `max` | `number` | `0`, `100` | Range. | | `format` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` | – | How `ProgressValue` formats the number. | | `getAriaValueText`| `(formatted: string, raw: number \| null) => string` | – | Human-readable value for assistive tech. | | `className` | `string` / state callback | – | Merged last; the default is a wrap layout. | ### `ProgressTrack`, `ProgressIndicator`, `ProgressLabel`, `ProgressValue` Plain wrappers over Base UI's parts; each forwards `className` and native props. `ProgressIndicator` carries the motion. ## Motion contract Recipe: `data.transition`, in both of its documented forms. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------- | | value change | `scaleX old → new` (one-shot) | `data.transition`| yes | | indeterminate | `opacity` pulse (continuous) | `data.transition`| yes | | reduced | value jumps; pulse kept, opacity only | `data.transition` | yes | | none | no transition, `animate-none` | – | – | The fill is a `scaleX` transform on an element that keeps the full track width, so a value change never triggers layout. Under `reduced` the fill jumps to the new value — position is information, the animation is not — while the indeterminate pulse survives, because opacity-only loading feedback is what M5 keeps. ## Keyboard interactions No keyboard interaction: the progress bar is not focusable. If the user can cancel the work, put a `button` next to it. ## Accessibility - Base UI puts `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuenow` on the root; `value={null}` omits `aria-valuenow`. - Give it a name with `aria-label`, or render `ProgressLabel` inside the root and let Base UI wire it. - Announce completion outside the bar (text or `toast`); a full bar is not announced by a screen reader on its own. - Never hide the percentage behind the animation: `ProgressValue` is the readable copy of the same fact. ## Responsive behavior The bar fills its container and stays 8px tall at every breakpoint. When it sits in a card header, keep the label and value on one line and let the bar take the next line — the default `flex-wrap` layout does this without extra classes. ## Performance One animated indicator per track. A determinate update uses a native transform animation; an indeterminate bar runs a CSS opacity loop. These do not animate layout, but whole-page frame performance still needs measurement. Avoid driving `value` from `requestAnimationFrame` yourself; pass the real value and let the transition smooth it. ## Notes for AI - `value` is required; pass `null` for indeterminate, never `undefined`. - Use `scaleX`, not width. A width transition relayouts the track every frame. - For work with no measurable end and no bar, use `spinner`, not a fake percentage.
